top_choice_rationale: Targeted protein degradation rests on one transferable principle, small-molecule induced proximity between an E3 ligase and a chosen protein, giving catalytic, sub-stoichiometric removal of targets that occupancy-based inhibitors cannot reach. Crews and Deshaies supplied the bifunctional design and Handa's cereblon identification explains the glue strand, so Crews, Deshaies and Handa form a defensible three-name citation written on the principle rather than on approved drugs. Its consequence is still partly prospective and Ciulli, Gray, Sakamoto, Kim and Ito are excluded, which is why lipid nanoparticles, with global clinical scale, follow as second choice.
